threads.thread_goal: Align on MVP scope, metrics, and event tracking spec before implementation starts.

messages.text: Kicking off the Unified Analytics Platform MVP for Product Usage Insights. For scope: we are limiting to two flagship products and top 10 events each, and we need to lock both the metrics list and the unified tracking spec before we touch implementation. I have drafted Unified Event Tracking Specification v1 in A1 and a first pass of the metrics and dashboards matrix in A2. Proposal: we use this thread to converge on the MVP metrics, validate that A2 matches expectations, and iterate on the event schema in A1 so we can call T1 ready to start. Please skim A1 and A2 and drop comments on missing metrics or confusing event definitions.

I went through A2 and tried to map each business question to a concrete metric. For the MVP, I see daily active users, weekly active users, feature adoption by cohort, and basic retention curves per product. One question: do we want to include funnel drop off for onboarding in the initial scope, or should that go into a later iteration to avoid stretching T1 and downstream modeling?

From a tracking perspective, onboarding funnels add a few more events and properties, but they are still within the top 10 per product if we are careful. In A1 I grouped events into auth, navigation, and feature usage. We could treat onboarding steps as a subset of feature usage and keep the count under control. That said, the derived funnel metrics might add complexity later, so maybe we track the events now but only commit to basic counts and not full funnel dashboards for the MVP.

Agree with tracking onboarding events now and keeping the MVP dashboard scope tighter. For metrics, I suggest we explicitly list: daily active users, weekly active users, 7 day retention, 30 day retention, feature adoption for top 5 features per product, and a simple onboarding completion rate. Funnels with step by step breakdown can live in the parking lot. I will update A2 to reflect that split so we can get sign off on the MVP list without blocking on more advanced views.

On A1, I noticed we have event names like productA_feature_clicked and productB_feature_clicked. Would it be better to use a shared naming pattern like feature_clicked with a product_id property, so that T1 does not diverge per product? That might simplify the ingestion and later the API, but I am not sure if there is any downside for the teams instrumenting the events.

If we use a shared event name like feature_clicked, would we still be able to tell which product and which feature it was in the warehouse? I assume we would add properties like product_key and feature_key, but I do not see them clearly listed in A1 yet. Maybe we should add a small example payload for each event type so implementation teams know exactly what to send.

Good catch. The intent is exactly that: shared event names with product_key, feature_key, and user_id_hash as properties. I will extend A1 with example payloads for each of the core events and a short section on naming conventions. That should make T1 clearer for the product teams and reduce the risk of inconsistent tracking between the two products.

On the metrics list you proposed, I would like to confirm how we define daily active users. Are we going with at least one qualifying event per day per anonymised user, or do we need a stricter definition like a session with a feature usage event? A2 currently mixes both wordings, so I want to avoid confusion when we validate dashboards later.

For simplicity in the MVP, I would define daily active users as at least one event of type session_started or feature_used per day per anonymised user. That aligns with how we plan to build the sessions and feature usage tables in T3 and keeps the definition consistent across products. We can document this explicitly in A2 under the metric definition for daily active users.

One more detail on A1: do we want to enforce validation rules on the client side, server side, or both? For example, making sure feature_key is never empty and that timestamps are in UTC. I am thinking ahead to T2 and T3, where bad data could cause issues in the transformations and dashboards.

We should define validation rules in A1 and enforce them at ingestion time in T2. Client side validation is nice to have but harder to guarantee across teams. For the MVP, I propose we implement server side checks for required fields, basic type validation, and a quarantine path for invalid events so they do not break downstream models. We can add a note in A1 that client teams are encouraged to mirror these checks.

If daily active users is based on session_started or feature_used, should we also count login events, or is that redundant? I am asking because some flows might only have a login and then a quick action that we do not track yet. Maybe we should clarify that in A1 so we do not miscount activity for those edge cases.

Good point. To keep the definition stable, I would not include pure login events in daily active users for now. Instead, we can ensure that the main post login screen emits a session_started event so that normal usage is captured. I will add a note in A1 and adjust the wording in A2 so that daily active users is always tied to session or feature activity, not just authentication.

With the latest updates, A1 now has shared event names, required properties, example payloads, and validation rules. A2 has the MVP metrics list with clear definitions and the onboarding completion metric marked as in scope. From my side, this is enough to start T1 and downstream work. Unless anyone sees a blocker, I suggest we mark the metrics list and tracking schema as approved for the MVP.

Summarising where we landed: metrics for the MVP are daily and weekly active users, 7 and 30 day retention, feature adoption for top 5 features per product, and onboarding completion rate, all defined in A2. Event tracking in A1 uses shared names with product_key and feature_key properties, example payloads, and ingestion side validation rules that will be implemented in T2. Funnels and more advanced views are explicitly out of scope for now. I am comfortable calling this the final MVP metrics list and tracking schema.

No objections from me. Locking this down will help us avoid scope creep later. I will start sketching how the ingestion code in T2 can validate against the A1 schema so we keep the data clean from day one.

All clear on my side as well. Having the examples in A1 and the definitions in A2 will make it easier to test the transformations later. I will keep an eye out for any inconsistencies once we start seeing real events, but I think we are good to proceed.

Thanks everyone. I will align with the product teams to share A1 and A2 and make sure they understand the conventions before they start instrumenting. If they raise any major concerns, I will bring them back here, but otherwise we can treat the spec as frozen for the MVP.

threads.thread_goal: Converge on architecture and pipeline design for ingestion and transformations.

messages.text: I have uploaded a first version of the Analytics Platform Architecture and Data Flow Design in A3. It outlines ingestion from product event streams into raw storage, transformations into clean analytics tables, and serving layers for dashboards and APIs. For this thread, we need to agree on the ingestion and transformation pattern for T2, T3, and T4, and also decide on the refresh frequency for the MVP. Please review A3 and comment on any concerns with the proposed architecture.

Looking at A3, I see you proposed a batch ingestion job that runs every 15 minutes and lands events into raw storage, then daily transformations for sessions, users, and feature usage. For T2, I can implement the ingestion as a scheduled job that reads from the event streams and writes to partitioned storage. One question: do we want to support near real time dashboards in the MVP, or is daily freshness enough for now?

From a usage perspective, most of the product and growth questions in A2 are fine with daily updates. Teams mainly want to see trends and retention, not minute by minute changes. If we try to do near real time now, we might complicate T3 and T4 with more complex dependency management. I would lean toward daily transformations for the MVP and revisit more frequent updates later.

On the transformation side, A3 suggests building core tables for sessions, users, and feature usage in T3, then semantic models for product and growth analytics in T4. I like the layered approach. One thing I want to clarify is how we handle late arriving events. If ingestion in T2 runs every 15 minutes but transformations are daily, do we need a small buffer window in the jobs so that events that arrive slightly late still get picked up correctly?

Yes, we should design T3 to be idempotent and to process a sliding window, for example the last two days of data, so that late events are incorporated. In A3 I proposed partitioning by event date and using a merge pattern in the transformations. That way, if ingestion in T2 delivers events slightly late, the next daily run will still reconcile them. We can document this in the job configs and in the runbook later.

I have a question about the semantic models in T4. A3 mentions dimensional models for users, features, and time. Are we planning to build separate models per product, or a single shared model with a product dimension? I want to make sure we do not duplicate work and that the dashboards can filter by product easily.

Given the unified tracking spec in A1, I think a shared semantic model with a product dimension makes more sense. That way, T4 can define common dimensions for users, features, and time, and the dashboards can slice by product without separate pipelines. It also keeps versioning simpler, since we only have one set of models to manage.

For T2, I can structure the raw storage so that events are partitioned by event_date and product_key, which should align well with the merge pattern you described for T3. I will also add basic monitoring for ingestion failures as per the T2 definition of done. If we stick with daily transformations, I will make sure the ingestion latency stays under 15 minutes so that the daily jobs always see a complete day.

If we go with daily transformations, do we want to schedule them at a specific time, for example 02:00 UTC, and communicate that as the data freshness expectation for the MVP? That would help set clear expectations for T5 and the dashboards, and we can reflect it in A3 and later in the runbook.

Yes, having a fixed daily schedule is important. I propose we run the main transformation pipeline in T3 at 02:00 UTC, after the bulk of the previous day events have landed. That gives us a clear data freshness statement: dashboards and the metrics API will reflect data up to the previous day by 03:00 UTC. I will update A3 to include this timing and the dependency chain between T2, T3, and T4.

Shared semantic models with a product dimension sound good. For T4, should we also version the models explicitly, like v1 for the MVP, so that future changes do not break existing dashboards or the metrics API? A3 mentions versioning briefly, but I am not sure how strict we want to be for the first release.

For the MVP, a simple versioning scheme should be enough. We can tag the core models in T4 as v1 in their names or metadata and document that in A3. Any breaking change later would require a new version, like v2, while keeping v1 around until consumers migrate. That keeps things predictable without over engineering the first iteration.

With the daily schedule at 02:00 UTC and the ingestion latency target, I think the architecture in A3 is clear enough for me to start implementing T2. I will also add logging and basic alerts so that if ingestion fails, we know before the T3 jobs run. That should help keep the pipelines reliable for the MVP.

From my side, the architecture pattern in A3, with batch ingestion into raw storage, daily transformations into clean tables in T3, and semantic models in T4, looks reasonable and fits our existing tooling. I do not see any blockers for the MVP. I support going ahead with this design and the daily refresh cadence.

To wrap up: we are choosing the architecture in A3 that uses scheduled ingestion in T2 into raw storage, daily transformation jobs in T3 to build sessions, users, and feature usage tables, and shared semantic models with a product dimension in T4, versioned as v1 for the MVP. Refresh frequency for the MVP will be daily, with the main pipeline running at 02:00 UTC and dashboards and APIs updated by 03:00 UTC. Unless there are last minute objections, I will treat this as our final architecture and refresh plan.

No objections here. The daily refresh and the chosen pattern in A3 should be more than enough for the MVP questions in A2. I will help validate the first runs of T3 and T4 once we have sample data flowing.

All clear. I will support with testing the semantic models in T4 once they are available and check that the product filters behave as expected. The daily schedule and versioning notes in A3 will help when we document this later.

threads.thread_goal: Define dashboard layout, KPIs, and performance expectations for the UI.

messages.text: I have shared the Dashboard Prototype and UX Wireframes in A8, aligned with the metrics list in A2. The main views cover daily and weekly active users, retention, feature adoption, and onboarding completion for both products. In this thread, we need to agree on the initial set of dashboard views and filters for T5, and confirm performance targets so we can plan T11 later. Please review A8 and comment on layout, KPIs, and any missing filters.

In A8, the overview tab shows daily active users and weekly active users by product, with a date range filter and a product selector. That matches A2 well. I would suggest adding a simple retention summary card on the overview, maybe 7 day retention for the last completed cohort, so that teams do not have to switch tabs just to see if retention is moving.

Overall the layout in A8 looks good to me. For the MVP, I would keep the number of tabs small: Overview, Retention, Feature Adoption, and Onboarding. Each tab should share the same basic filters: date range, product, and maybe platform if we have that in the events. That will keep T5 focused and make performance tuning in T11 easier.

From an implementation angle for T5, reusing the same filter components across tabs will help with performance and maintainability. If we standardise on date range and product filters, plus an optional feature selector on the Feature Adoption tab, we can cache some of the underlying queries and make it easier to hit the under 5 seconds target that T11 will focus on.

On the Retention tab in A8, do we want to show both 7 day and 30 day retention curves, or just one for the MVP? Showing both might be useful, but it could also slow down the page if the queries are heavy. Maybe we can start with 7 day retention and add 30 day later if stakeholders ask for it.

I would prioritise 7 day retention for the MVP, since it reacts faster to product changes. We can still compute 30 day retention in the models, but we do not need to visualise it yet. That keeps the Retention tab in A8 simpler and should help with performance for T5 and T11.

I can update A8 so that the Overview tab includes a small 7 day retention summary card, using the same definition as in A2. That should not add much complexity to T5, since the data will already be available from the semantic models. For filters, I will standardise on date range and product across all tabs, plus feature selector on Feature Adoption and maybe a simple segment selector later if we have time.

On performance targets, the project constraints say dashboards must load in under 5 seconds for standard queries. For the MVP, I suggest we define standard queries as: Overview tab with default date range of last 30 days, Retention tab with 7 day retention for the last 8 cohorts, Feature Adoption tab for top 5 features, and Onboarding tab for the last 30 days. T11 can then focus on tuning these specific cases.

Those standard cases sound reasonable. For T5, I will design the queries to aggregate at the right grain so we do not pull raw events into the dashboard. Using the semantic models from T4 should help a lot. When we get to T11, we can profile the slowest queries and add indexes or pre aggregated tables if needed.

For filters, should we also support a quick preset like last 7 days and last 30 days, instead of only a free date range picker? That might reduce the number of heavy custom queries and make it easier to stay within the 5 second target.

Good idea. I will adjust A8 so that the default is last 30 days, with quick presets for last 7 days and last 90 days, and keep the custom range as an advanced option. That should help T5 keep the common paths fast while still allowing flexibility when needed.

To summarise the views: Overview with daily and weekly active users plus a 7 day retention summary, Retention tab with 7 day retention curves, Feature Adoption tab with adoption for top 5 features and a feature selector, and Onboarding tab with completion rate. All tabs share date range and product filters, with quick presets. That feels like a solid MVP set without overextending T5.

Agreed. With that set of views and filters, we cover all the MVP metrics in A2 and keep the implementation in T5 manageable. For performance, we are aligning on under 5 seconds load time for the standard queries you listed, with data freshness of daily as defined in A3. I suggest we lock this as the initial dashboard scope and performance targets for the MVP.

Sounds good to me. I will start implementing the Overview and Retention tabs in T5 first, using the agreed filters and metrics, and we can iterate on performance once we have real data to test with in T11.

No concerns from my side. The quick presets and limited number of tabs should help keep things responsive. I can help test the dashboards once T5 has a first version, focusing on the standard queries we defined for T11.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on access control, anonymisation, and compliance requirements.

messages.text: Following up on the privacy constraints for the Unified Analytics Platform MVP, I have linked the Data Access and Anonymisation Policy in A5 and the draft Operational Runbook in A6. We need to agree on the access roles, anonymisation rules for analytics data in T8, and how we document incident handling in T9. The security officer has asked that we confirm the approach here before implementation. Please review A5 and share any concerns or gaps.

In A5, the proposal is to store only anonymised user identifiers in the analytics layers, with user_id_hash derived from a one way hash of the internal user id plus a salt. Direct identifiers like email and full name are excluded from the analytics warehouse. That seems aligned with the project constraints. One question: do we ever need to re identify users for debugging, or should that be strictly out of scope for this platform?

Given the constraints, I would keep re identification out of scope for the analytics platform. If debugging requires user level investigation, that should happen in the operational systems with appropriate access controls, not in the analytics warehouse. A5 already hints at this separation, but we can make it explicit so T8 does not accidentally include any direct identifiers.

On access roles, A5 defines three main groups: analytics_admin, analytics_power_user, and analytics_viewer. For T8, I can map these to our existing identity provider roles and configure role based access for the dashboards and warehouse schemas. I just want to confirm that only analytics_admin can see raw event tables, while power users and viewers are limited to the curated models.

Yes, that is the intent. Raw event tables should be restricted to analytics_admin only, since they may contain more detailed metadata even if user ids are anonymised. Power users and viewers should work exclusively with the curated models defined in T4. I will update A5 to state this clearly so that the security officer can review and sign off.

In A6, the runbook mentions incident classification for data access issues, but it is a bit high level. For T9, should we define specific steps for what to do if someone reports that they can see data they should not, for example a role misconfiguration? I want to make sure we have a clear escalation path.

Good point. For T9, we can extend A6 with a specific playbook for access incidents: immediately revoke the affected role or account, capture logs of the access, notify the security officer, and then review and fix the role configuration. We should also document how to verify that anonymisation rules in T8 are still applied correctly after any change.

On anonymisation in T8, A5 lists user_id_hash and a few coarse grained attributes like country and platform. Do we need to further bucket any numeric fields, like session duration, to avoid edge cases where a single user could be identified by a very unique pattern? Or is that considered low risk for the MVP given the aggregation level in the dashboards?

For the MVP, I think we can keep numeric fields like session duration as is in the warehouse, but ensure that dashboards and the metrics API only expose aggregated values, not raw per user records. A5 already states that only aggregated and anonymised data is exposed to consumers. If the security officer later requests additional bucketing, we can adjust T8 accordingly.

For T8 implementation, I will make sure that any PII fields from the source streams are either dropped or transformed before they reach the analytics layers. I will also add checks in the ingestion and transformation code so that if a new field that looks like PII appears, we log it and fail the pipeline until it is reviewed. We can document this behaviour in A6 under monitoring.

That makes sense. For T9, I can help draft the incident escalation steps in A6, including who to notify and how to record the incident. I will also add a short section on how to use the monitoring dashboards to check for unusual access patterns, even if we keep it simple for the MVP.

With the current wording in A5 and the planned checks in T8 and T9, I think we meet the privacy requirements for the MVP: anonymised user ids, no direct identifiers in analytics, role based access with restricted raw tables, and documented incident handling in A6. I do not see any major gaps, but we should send the updated A5 and A6 to the security officer for final review.

Agreed. To summarise: A5 defines anonymisation via user_id_hash and removal of direct identifiers, with raw tables restricted to analytics_admin and curated models for other roles. T8 will enforce these rules in the pipelines and add checks for unexpected PII. A6 and T9 will document monitoring and incident response, including specific steps for access incidents. I will send A5 and A6 to the security officer for sign off and treat their approval as the final go ahead on the access model and anonymisation rules.

Once the security officer confirms A5 and A6, I will update any references in the dashboard specs so that T5 clearly states which roles can access which views. That should avoid confusion when we roll out the MVP.

threads.thread_goal: Plan launch, validate readiness, and capture follow-ups after MVP go-live.

messages.text: We are approaching the end of the 21 day window for the Unified Analytics Platform MVP. I have linked the MVP Launch Readiness Checklist in A4, the Historical Data Backfill ticket in A7, and the Operational Runbook draft in A6. Proposal: we target the MVP launch for next Wednesday, pending completion of T10 and T12 items in A4. In this thread, we need to confirm the launch date, check readiness, and list follow ups for after go live.

I went through A4 and most of the core items look green: ingestion and transformations are running daily, dashboards are within the 5 second target for standard queries, and access controls from T8 are in place. The main open items I see are the historical backfill in T10 and the demo and Q and A session in T12. A7 shows that the backfill is partially complete for one product. Do we have an ETA for finishing the second product and validating counts?

For T10, the backfill for Product A is done and validated against source counts, as noted in A7. For Product B, the load is running now and should finish by end of day. After that, I need a few hours to run completeness checks and spot check trends. Barring surprises, I am confident we can mark T10 as done by tomorrow.

On T12, I can prepare a short demo that walks through the Overview, Retention, Feature Adoption, and Onboarding tabs, and shows how the metrics align with A2. We should also capture common questions during the session and add them to the runbook in A6. I can host the demo on Tuesday so we have a day to react before the proposed Wednesday launch.

In A4, there is an item about incident escalation paths being documented. I have added the access incident playbook to A6 as part of T9, but we still need to confirm who is on call for the first week after launch. Do we want a lightweight rotation among us, or should we ask the wider engineering team to take that on after a short handover?

For the first week after launch, I suggest we keep on call within this project group so we can react quickly to any issues. After that, we can hand over to the wider engineering on call rotation, using A6 and T9 as the reference. I will note this in A4 under the launch plan and confirm with our manager so they are aware of the temporary arrangement.

Once the Product B backfill finishes, I can help validate trends against the source system and sanity check retention curves. That should give us more confidence before we mark T10 as complete in A4. If we find any discrepancies, we can decide quickly whether they are data issues or just differences in definitions.

Sounds good. I will ping you once the load completes and the initial checks pass. I will also update A7 with any assumptions or edge cases we encounter during the backfill so that future runs have a clear reference.

For the demo in T12, I will prepare a short checklist based on A4 so we can walk through each readiness item live: data freshness, dashboard performance, access controls, and runbook availability. That should make it easier for stakeholders to see that we are ready for launch.

I am ok being part of the initial on call group. Once we see how stable the pipelines are, we can adjust the runbook in A6 with any lessons learned and then hand over to the wider team as you suggested.

Given the current status in A4 and the plan for T10 and T12, I think next Wednesday is a realistic launch date, assuming the backfill completes tomorrow and the demo on Tuesday does not surface any critical issues. We should also capture a small v2 backlog during or right after the demo, as required by T12.

Agreed. During the T12 demo, we will explicitly ask stakeholders for any must have follow ups and record them as v2 items, separate from the MVP scope in A4. That way, the launch decision is based on the current checklist, not on new requests that come up in the meeting.

One more thing from A4: we should run a quick rollback test in staging before launch, as part of T7, to make sure we can revert if something goes wrong. I know T7 is mostly done, but I want to double check that the rollback step is actually exercised before we go live.
Good call. I will schedule a quick rollback test in staging tomorrow and update A4 once it is done. That will close out the remaining T7 item on the checklist.

After the demo, I can also send a short summary email to stakeholders with links to the dashboards, A6 for the runbook, and a note on who to contact for issues during the first week. That should help with the communication part of T12.

Once T10 is marked complete and the rollback test is done, I will do a final pass over A4 to ensure all items are green. If everything checks out, I see no reason not to proceed with the Wednesday launch.

Based on the current status and plans: T10 backfill will be complete and validated by tomorrow, T7 rollback test will run in staging tomorrow, and T12 demo and comms will happen on Tuesday. Assuming no critical issues arise, I propose we confirm next Wednesday as the MVP launch date and mark A4 as go once those items are done. I will communicate this plan to the product stakeholders and treat this as our go decision for the MVP launch.
Works for me. I will stay available during and after the launch window to help monitor the dashboards and pipelines, and update A6 with any issues we encounter so that the runbook stays accurate.
